newsitem.title: UK: EMI shares rebound after results.
newsitem.headline: EMI shares rebound after results.

text.p: Shares in EMI Group Plc clawed back initial losses on Tuesday to be trading higher after third quarter results.
The shares were up 27p at 12.20 stg by 1010 GMT after earlier slipping by as much as 35p in pre-market trade in reaction to lower than expected nine month results.
"The number was not far from what people were expecting and the shares were off yesterday as well," said SocGen analyst Jason Crisp.
The shares finished 42p lower on Monday in anticipation of disappointing profits.
"The results were clearly not very good, but not a disaster," Crisp said. "The statement was reasonably upbeat."
Group operating profit excluding exceptional items fell to 293.3 million stg from 312.4 million stg a year earlier. Analysts had been expecting profits in the range of 326-377 million stg.

"If you separate the third quarter then the results are even more dramatic, with music sales down 18 percent," Crisp said. "But the damage was done mainly in the U.S where profits were half that of last year."
EMI later said that full-year profits were expected to be in the range of 380-400 million stg. Crisp was expecting profits of around 410 million stg before today's results.
The group said that its release schedule was more heavily weighted than usual towards the final quarter this year and so far sales in the fourth quarter were in line with expectations.
